advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix marker name/reason splitting so step names containing a whitespace-surrounded separator (em dash) remain justifiable — e.g. split on the LAST separator, or require an explicit reason delimiter.
evidence: `split = _NAME_REASON_RE.search(rest)` — first whitespace-surrounded separator wins (markers.py:83-85)
`_SEPARATORS = ("—", "--", "-", ":")` (markers.py:42)

Committed baseline step names that embed ` — `: `ci_gate::.github/workflows/release.yml::Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main`, `ci_gate::.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml::mypy — full library + scripts/ (gating)`, `ci_gate::.github/workflows/mirror-guard.yml::mirror-guard — replication health (Gerrit vs GitHub main SHA)`
The parser handles the flag-in-name case (test_a_marker_admits_a_step_whose_name_carries_a_flag) but not the separator-in-name case.
advisory.finding: The marker parser cannot justify any workflow-step mechanism whose name contains a whitespace-surrounded separator. `_split_name_reason` splits at the FIRST match of `_NAME_REASON_RE` (which matches ` — `/` -- `/` - `/` : `), so a marker for a step named e.g. `Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main` truncates the harvested name to `...::Guard`, producing a key that never matches the real `ci_gate::…::Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main` mechanism.
scenarios: An author needs to justify a change touching the `Guard — HEAD is an ancestor of origin/main` step; every marker they write is parsed as name=`Guard`, reason=`HEAD is an ancestor…`, so the gate never admits the actual key and the mechanism is un-justifiable short of renaming the step.

coaching.coaching: Add a regression test covering duplicate step-name collision in workflow census.
coaching.subject: duplicate step-name collision in workflow census

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Disambiguate duplicate step labels within a single workflow (e.g. append the step's line/index) so co-named `run:` steps do not collapse to one census entry.
evidence: `sites.append((f"{rel}::{named[0]}", path, named[1]))` keyed only on workflow path + step label (detect_ci.py:120)
census flattens to a set-like dict keyed by `<kind>::<name>` (check_mechanism_delta.py:141-143), so duplicate labels within one file coalesce
Unnamed steps are named by a 60-char run snippet (detect_ci.py:80-83), so two long commands sharing a 60-char prefix also collide.
dropped.finding: Within a single workflow file, two `run:` steps that share a `name:` (or, when unnamed, the same first `run:` line truncated to 60 chars) collapse to one `<workflow>::<name>` census key. This is the exact partition-violation the design guards against for config keys (section-qualification), but it is unguarded for the YAML-step shape: a second identical-named step in the same workflow is added for free.
scenarios: A workflow gains a second step named identically to an existing one (common for repeated `Configure git identity` / `Wait for … to become ready` labels inside one file) — the census count is unchanged, so no `new` bucket fires and the added gate step escapes the ratchet.
